timeline.claim: The presenters selected approximately 566.39 as the upside OMG boundary and 564.50 as the downside boundary after moving the upside trigger beyond nearby right-shoulder resistance.
The source described a double-bottom support response while acknowledging that all referenced moving averages remained above price and were falling.
For the downside OMG, the source prescribed a close below the boundary followed by a bounce and rollover rather than first-penetration entry.
The source reported ten 566 calls at 6.66 at a stated 9:41 a.m. while describing the entry as aggressive.
The source reported entering the downside OMG puts at 6.52 at a stated 9:43 a.m.; surrounding context indicates May 16 564 puts, but the strike cue is garbled.
The source set the OMG premium target at 6.91, linked to approximately SPY 563.80-563.85.
The source reported a 6.91 OMG fill and characterized it as a five-minute trade.
The source waited for the calls to recover through the EMAs while simultaneously identifying further downside room toward clustered support.
Asked whether to exit the calls, the source chose to hold, stated a 7.12 cost and 7.50 sell order, and described the selloff as temporary without giving a stop.
The first one-minute 50-MA break was rejected on the highest one-minute volume since the open; price later held the 10/20 MAs and challenged a descending trend line.
A presenter reported May 16 564 calls at 7.51 with a 7.84 target linked to SPY just below 565.
The original ten 566 calls at 6.66 were restated with a 7.00 sell order and an underlying target around SPY 565.60.
The source reported the 564-call target filled at 7.84; shortly afterward it said the other target also filled, though caption-only position pairing is partly ambiguous.
The source said the OMG worked and reported the pick-of-the-day 566 calls were down about one dollar near recording end, with no resolved outcome.

claims.label: OMG_CLOSE_BOUNCE_ROLLOVER_ENTRY
claims.claim: The source used a close below the OMG boundary, a bounce, and a renewed rollover as the downside entry sequence.
claims.disconfirming_evidence_required: Deterministic OMG labels, synchronized SPY bars, executable option marks, fills, costs, and first-touch and first-close baseline replays.

claims.label: STRUCTURAL_ROOM_TRIGGER_FILTER
claims.claim: The presenters moved the upside trigger beyond nearby right-shoulder resistance because the initial level left insufficient room.
claims.disconfirming_evidence_required: Deterministic resistance and room-to-target labels with timestamped bars, option marks, costs, and out-of-sample replay.

claims.label: PRE_EVENT_AGGRESSIVE_CALL_BELOW_FALLING_MAS
claims.claim: The source entered bullish calls before the scheduled event while price remained below falling moving averages and later held through adverse movement without a stated invalidation.
claims.disconfirming_evidence_required: Synchronized bars, exact event timestamp, option bid/ask path, fill, MFE/MAE, time-underwater, and a post-event-confirmation baseline.

claims.label: FAILED_MA_BREAK_THEN_ACCEPTED_RECOVERY
claims.claim: A failed 50-MA break was followed by a 10/20-MA hold, trend-line break, retest, and renewed upside move before the later 564-call trade.
claims.disconfirming_evidence_required: Deterministic MA and trend-line labels, synchronized bars, executable option marks, fills, MFE/MAE, and first-break and no-retest baselines.

claims.label: SIMULTANEOUS_OPPOSING_OPTION_LEGS
claims.claim: The source carried opposing call and put positions without reporting aggregate delta, combined maximum loss, or leg-specific invalidations.
claims.disconfirming_evidence_required: Contract-level fills, synchronized Greeks, combined P&L, per-leg MFE/MAE, fees, and explicit portfolio risk limits.
